text: Arts Seal is a debuff in and . It disables the use of all arts except for Talent Arts. Auto-attacks are still useable through this debuff, as are Double Attacks and Counterattacks. This debuff is a complement to Paralysis, which cripples auto-attacking capabilities. In the , this debuff can be noticed via glowing purple chain-like rings over the character or enemy that is under it.

Atomizek Ansels (Japanese: , Atomizeku Anseru) are enemies in . They are members of the Ansel family, and can be found at level 46 around the Sealed Tower on Valak Mountain at night. They can drop Ansel Fish Pies, which are needed for A Gift For Miko.

The Audience Chamber (Japanese: , Ekken no Ma) is a location in . It is located on the second floor of Alcamoth. It is linked by teleporters to the Ascension Hall and the Revelation Hall. Kallian, Sorean and Lorithia can be found here the first time the party visits Alcamoth, but after the events at Mechonis Core it is guarded by eight Arel Telethia. It is also the location of Telethia Donnis. A Heart-to-Heart - "So Close, Yet So Far" - is located here.

Art Points, commonly referred to as AP, are a game mechanic in and , similar to EXP and SP; however, instead of being used immediately to level up characters, they are left for the player to manually level up the wanted arts, and can be saved for as long as desired. AP can be earned by defeating enemies and discovering Landmarks. In the , AP can also be earned by scanning an amiibo. Using AP to level up Arts increases their effectiveness. What this means is different for every Art, however; damage-dealing Arts will increase in power upon leveling, and all Arts (excluding the Monado Arts) will be granted shortened Cooldown times. Added effects may also become more potent upon leveling up, tho

Astral Crusader (known as Star Crusader in the Japanese version) is a Class featured in . This class provides bonuses to ranged attack and accuracy. It uses Sniper Rifle and Javelin as its weapons. It is one of six final classes and can only be leveled up from Partisan Eagle.

Assister Quos (Japanese: , Ashisuto Kuō) are two Story and Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Quo machines, Ganglion's flying robots, and can be found at level 28 at the NLA Primary Defense Line in Primordia during Chapter 8. They assist Pursuit Qmoevas and Blitz Qmoevas when the Ganglion attack the East Gate of New Los Angeles.

Atop the Giant Ring (Japanese: , Koware Kyodai Ringu Chōjō, Broken Giant Ring Summit) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, on top of the largest ring structure. It can be reached in a Skell with the Flight Module upwards from FN Site 312, but can also be reached without a Skell from multiple unconventional ascent routes. As with all Scenic Viewpoints, its discovery yields an achievement ("Atop the Giant Ring"). There are no enemies here, but a few Collectibles, as well as an indigen nest requiring level 5 Biological Field-Skill to open.

Auto-Attack Damage is a character stat in Xenoblade Chronicles which determines the amount of Damage dealt by Auto-Attacks and physical Battle Arts. It displayed as a minimum value and a maximum value separated by a hyphen, for example "586–657". Auto-Attack Damage is calculated by adding the character's Strength to the equipped weapon's Attack, including the effects of any gems or skills which improve those stats. Whenever a character auto-attacks or uses a physical art, the game chooses a random value between that character's minimum and maximum Auto-Attack Damage values, which it then uses to calculate the damage. However, due to a bug the random value can never exceed the minimum+99. Bec

Artifices (Japanese: , Debaisu) are powerful machines in and . They are meant to be used by Aegises. Many of them were used by Malos during the Aegis War, to fight against Mythra, the Titans, and the Blades. Artifices mostly resemble gargantuan humanoid mechs. Although the Artifices may be used by any Aegis, Mythra and Pyra are particularly affiliated with Artifice Ophion, while Malos is able to command Gargoyles. Both Mythra and Malos are able to control their own Siren.

Assault Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Sakuraba Industries Assault Rifle. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Relics category of the Primordia Collectopedia. The Assault weapons available in-game are: * Combat Assault Rifle * Delta Assault Rifle * Destroyer Assault Rifle * Ophidian Assault Rifle * Storm Assault Rifle * Striker Assault Rifle * Warrior Assault Rifle

Assault III Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Sakuraba Industries Assault Rifle. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Turf War. The Assault III weapons available in-game are: * Storm Assault Rifle III * Soldier Assault Rifle III * Warrior Assault Rifle III * Ophidian Assault Rifle III * Destroyer Assault Rifle III * Striker Assault Rifle III * Delta Assault Rifle III * Cosmic Assault Rifle III * Nebulan Assault Rifle III * Ultra Nebulan Assault Rifle III

Assailer Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Candid & Credible Assault Rifle. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Murder Most Foul, alongside the I <3 Pizza holofigure. The Assailer weapons available in-game are: * Storm Assailer * Soldier Assailer * Warrior Assailer * Ophidian Assailer * Destroyer Assailer * Striker Assailer * Delta Assailer * Original Assailer * Cosmic Assailer * Nebulan Assailer

Assault II Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Sakuraba Industries Assault Rifle. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Xenotech category of the Sylvalum Collectopedia. The Assault II weapons available in-game are: * Storm Assault Rifle II * Soldier Assault Rifle II * Warrior Assault Rifle II * Ophidian Assault Rifle II * Destroyer Assault Rifle II * Striker Assault Rifle II * Delta Assault Rifle II * Cosmic Assault Rifle II * Nebulan Assault Rifle II

Auras are special beneficiary buffs in and . Many auras are unique in their effect and some are unique to certain characters or enemies and unlike other buffs. Some abilities requires a certain aura to be active before they can be used. Unlike other buffs, the caster can only have one aura at a time; activating another aura will remove the previous one. Arts that are categorised as Auras are orange in colour, although some are Talent Arts. The Daze and Aura Seal debuffs remove auras and prevent casting them. Melia's Mind Blast also removes auras from enemies.

Aura Burst (Japanese: , Ōrabāsuto) is one of Reyn's Ether arts in . It can only be used when he has an aura active. It is a medium-range attack that hits enemies within 10 meters, generating volatile aggro and inflicting a Strength Down 25% debuff on all enemies hit. In , Nene has an identical version of this art called Aura Toast.

Aspids (Japanese: , Asupīdo) are a family of enemies in and . They are flying, eel-like creatures sporting thin wing-like appendages which often appear after Salvaging. All Aspids have the same appearance except for the Rabres Aspid, which uses the model of a red Lexos. Similarly, the Blizzard Lexos uses an Aspid model.

Arrest Warrant (Japanese: , Shimeitehaihan no Hobaku) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector", "Transport Mastery" and "Fortitude" Field Skills.

Art Supplies is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya by talking to Doghant, who paints on a balcony overlooking the Commercial District, when the nation has at least 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 80 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 20 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Keen Eye", "Production Mastery" and "Mineralogy" Field Skills.
Asset Scouts (Japanese: , Asetto Sukauto) are enemies in . They are members of Lindwurm, and can be found at level 40-44 at the Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago.
Arogan Rhoguls (Japanese: , Arogan Rōguru) are enemies in . They are members of the Rhogul family, and can be found at level 29-31 at the Old City of Teddim in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

At the Seat of Power is a Heart-to-Heart in . It takes place in the Throne Room of Hardhaigh Palace. Aegaeon wants to ask Emperor Niall why he has not allowed him to read the histories. The two options to choose between are "As a sign of demotion." and "So I'd save the world, not the Empire.". Viewing this Heart-to-Heart is required to unlock Aegaeon's level 4 "Serene Heart" Battle Skill.
At Wit's End is a quest in . It can be received from Sokoko on Merto Island in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Auresco, or Auresco, Royal Capital (Japanese: , Ōto Aururiumu, Aurulium, Royal Capital) is the capital city of the Kingdom of Torna, and a location that appears in . It is the northernmost area on the Tornan Titan, and connects only to the Dannagh Region. The majority of the NPCs in the game live here, and there are no enemies in this area except those encountered in Story or Quest events.

The Auresco, Main Gate (Japanese: , Ōto Aururiumu Seimon) is a landmark in . It is located in the southern area of the city, and serves as its main entrance from Planus Bridge. There are no enemies here.

The Auresco, Rear Gate (Japanese: , Ōto Aururiumu Uramon) is a landmark in . It is located in the eastern area of Auresco, in the Orem Storage Ward, and once unlocked (during story progression) leads out of the city to an elevator that descends to Torna's Womb.
Astelle Harbor (Japanese: , Asuteru-kō) is a Landmark in . It is located in the City. After Chapter 5, the party can travel to Farview Cape in Erythia Sea from here.

Artificial Optho (Japanese: , Kyozō no Oputo) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Droid, and can be found at level 69 in the Origin Interior, in the Hangar, Upper Level. It forms the quatuor "Hollow Ones" with Vapid Roger, Dishonest Karom and Phony Temnos. The "Magic Transmutation" Skill can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Armadillos (Japanese: , Āmadiro) are enemies in . They are Agnian Levnises. Two Quest Exclusive Bosses can be found at level 29 at Great Cotte Falls in the Pentelas Region during Unwavering Resolve. They also can be found at level 54 in Farlaine Underpass in Erythia Sea during Side Story: Taion and in the City during Side Story: Sena. Three are also fought at level 68 alongside Dorrick on the Terra Wastelands of Ribbi Flats during The Final Cog.

Bad Timing (Japanese: , Baddo Taimingu) is a quest in . It can be received from a trapped Nopon Researcher in Valak Mountain, in the northern part of the Great Glacier region. The Magma Rock is required to melt the Thick Ice Wall. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.

Banquet Biters (Japanese: , Kanshoku no Kamukamu) are Unique weapons in . They are biters wielded by Riki, and can be obtained from numerous high-level enemies. They are not otherwise available. As a Unique Weapon, it is similar to Melia's High Entia Soul, giving the player three free gems with which to improve status effects. Banquet Biters have the ability to damage Mechon although it is not explicitly indicated whether this weapon can damage Mechon or is built from Mechonis parts like for usual "Anti-Mechon" or "Machina" weapons series.

Beast Biters (Japanese: , Kemono no Kamukamu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters wielded by Riki. They can be acquired by purchasing them at the Melfica Road Shop in Alcamoth, and both the Zokhed Pass Shop and the Nopon Camp Shop on Valak Mountain for 18,480 G.
Bagnar Snowfield (Japanese: , Bajīna setsugen) is a location in . It is located on the upper level of Valak Mountain, on the northwest end of the map. The Hollow Bone is in the middle of the field.
Bargs (Japanese: , Bōku) are enemies in . They are quadrupedal unicorn-like enemies that are only found on Prison Island during the final chapter of the game.
Babel Deinoses (Japanese: , Berubēru Dinosu) are enemies in . They are members of the Deinos family, and can be found at level 75 on Prison Island in the Banquet Hall and on Gravina Bridge.
Babeli Bargs (Japanese: , Baberi Bōku) are enemies in . They are members of the Barg family, and can be found at level 74-76 on Prison Island.

The Battle Arena (Japanese: , Shinpan no Tōgijō) is a location in . It is first known as the "Arena", and is located on the second floor of Prison Island when it is revisited. It connects to the Behemoth Nest, and is renamed the "Battle Arena" when Dickson drops the Arena down a level.

Balgas Lungs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Caura Balgas and Fiendish Auburn on Prison Island, and can not be traded for. According to their description, it is said that these ten metre lungs can store air forever.

Balaenas (Japanese: , Baraena) are Piscinoid enemies in . They are flying baleen whale-like creatures with two sac-like organs attached to their backs and are similar to Cetos in appearance. They can be found in Primordia and Oblivia and their surrounding waters.

Beach Xiphias (Japanese: , Bīchi Rumederu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Xiphias family, and can be found at level 16-17 in Noctilum and Noctilum Waters, in particular the small island located southwest of FN Site 209.

Battle Points, also known as BP, are a mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are used to raise the level of Arts and Skills. Battle Points are earned in a number of ways: * Raising one's Level or Class Rank * Discovering Base Camps * Opening Treasure Boxes * Registering "Lucky Panel" collectibles (marked with a star) in the Collectopedia * Completing rows, categories, and regions of collectibles in the Collectopedia * Completing Squad Missions * Completing "EXP and BP" Support Missions The total BP cost to level a standard non-Tension Art to its maximum is 124 BP, while it costs 186 BP for a Tension Art. The total BP needed to max out a Skill is 62 BP. Most sources of BP are automatically

Barbed Remote Qmoevas (Japanese: , Taronrimōto Kumūba) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Qmoeva machines, and can be found at level 31 or level 36-37 in Primordia Waters, north of the big island.

Avagar Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Grenada Galactic Group Assault Rifle. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Xenotech category of the Noctilum Collectopedia. The Avagar weapons available in-game are: * Storm Avagar * Soldier Avagar * Warrior Avagar * Ophidian Avagar * Destroyer Avagar * Striker Avagar * Delta Avagar * Cosmic Avagar * Nebulan Avagar

Bangbangs Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Nopon Commerce Guild Dual Guns. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Setting Forth. The Bangbangs weapons available in-game are: * Storm Bangbangs * Soldier Bangbangs * Warrior Bangbangs * Ophidian Bangbangs * Destroyer Bangbangs * Striker Bangbangs * Delta Bangbangs * Original Bangbangs * Cosmic Bangbangs * Nebulan Bangbangs
B-Bombs are shoulder weapons for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Qmoevas bosses or by destroying Qmoevas' weapon appendages.

Baldotas Isle (Japanese: , Barudotasu-tō) is a landmark in . It is an island located in the Rigitte Waters of the Leftherian Archipelago, accessible from Rigitte Harbor, and is linked by walkways to Daridan's Stack and Daram Isle.
The Azure Schoolhouse (Japanese: , Tenshoku no Manabiya) is a Landmark in . It is located on Fonsett Island of the Leftherian Archipelago. It is unlocked after School is in Session is completed.

Bathein Watchtower (Japanese: , Bazuain Miharitō) is a landmark in . It is located in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain, and serves as a watchpost over the city and the Upper Level of Mor Ardain. There is a wire that connects the top of the tower to Alba Cavanich. It is possible to slide on this wire and ride it to the town. There are no enemies here except during The Lone Watchman.

Avoiding Heavy Losses (Japanese: , Daisongai no Kaihi) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild, and is unlocked automatically when the Garfont Mercenaries reach Merc Level 2 and the nation has at least 2 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Transport Mastery" and "Info Collector" Field Skills.

Beat the Heat is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector", "Icecraft" and "Ice Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Grumbird Rice Bowl in Platini Deli * Snow Dumplings in Placks Patisserie
The Basement Key is a Key Item in . It is given to the player by Zadazan at the Island Base Lindwurm in the Leftherian Archipelago, after defeating him in battle during the quest Bana's Revenge.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Beast-Hide Vests (Japanese: , Jūhi no Beruto) are DLC accessories in . They increase the wearer's Strength stat by up to 37%. They are the upgraded version of the Steam Belt, Silver Belt, and Ceramic Belt accessories. They can be found in the Land of Challenge from Treasure Troves obtained after completing a Challenge Battle, available as downloadable content from the Challenge Battle Mode Pack of the Expansion Pass. For a similar additive effect that can stack with this gear, check the Muscle Belt and Champion Belt accessories.

Barney Stones are objects in . They are a set of four glowing blue crystals set on low pillars in caves around the Kingdom of Torna, rumored to have been set up by an ancient adventurer named Barney and first encountered during Barmy Tale of Barney. When activated, Barney Stones spawn three waves of progressively stronger monsters which must be defeated. Upon defeat of the third wave, the stone shatters and a Treasure Trove is unearthed from the ground. These troves always contain a blueprint alongside gold and items. Titan Antibody Cores, four similar crystals in the Tornan Titan Interior, have identical mechanics - although these lift barriers upon completion rather than deposit Treasure T

Barouh Plaza (Japanese: , Beruu Hiroba) is a landmark in . It is located on the Bionis' Shoulder, east of Cinnabar Plateau. There are two paths from here continuing west; the upper leads through Barouh Ruins Cave to the floating Soltnar Seal Island, and the lower leads through Thulles Way towards Gran Dell.

Balquors Gate (Japanese: , Barukurusu Gēto) is a Location in . It is located on the Urayan Trail in the Pentelas Region. It is located east of Mountain Front: Keves. The gate connecting it to Engardo Pass can be opened after defeating Moebius O & P.

Barbed Merod (Japanese: , Kyōshin no Nirudo) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Urchon family, and can be found at level 51 at Anu Shoals in Erythia Sea, or on an island north of the Seaspray Lookout. The "Needle Shell" Skill can be earned by the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Axel is an NPC in . He is a City Survivor who is initally found on the Oracle Spire at The Ragmos Desolation. After being rescued, he moves to Colony 9 to be with his little sister, Finley. Axel's Community is gained when talking to him after completing the quest The Junior Workforce.

Basverg Belfry (Japanese: , Basuburuku Shōrō) is a location in . It is located on the fifth floor of Prison Island, and is only accessible during the second visit. It is accessed by crossing Travalga Bridge from the Corridor of Silence. Inside is a spiral staircase that leads to the upper platform. A bell is hanging atop and is rung by activating the Dragon Summon switch. When it is rung, a dragon is summoned in the Corridor of Silence, west of Gondorl Cathedral.

Behemoths (Japanese: , Behimosu) are powerful monsters in the , appearing in and . All Behemoths use the same model, although Behemoths in have glowing blue lines all over them whilst Behemoths in lack these. They bear a strong resemblance to Mammuts.
Black Peonies (Japanese: , Kurobotan) are collectables in . They can be found at Valak Mountain. According to their description, when a petal falls, they emit a sound that makes the heart leap.
Black Ashes (Japanese: , Burakku Asshu) are collectables in . They can be found on Valak Mountain. According to their description, they are textured stones made up of lumps of charcoal.
Bitter Melons (Japanese: , Nigameron) are collectables in . They can be found in Sword Valley and Colony 6. According to their description, their tangy taste strengthens as they ripen.

Bellflower Crystals (Japanese: , Kikyou Kurisutaru) are collectables in . They can be found in Agniratha and Colony 6. According to their description, they are quartz flowers that let their petals fly in a wonderful way when picked.

The Bionis' Thumb (Japanese: , Kyoshin no Oyayubi) is a landmark in . It is the first landmark in Sword Valley, and consists of a tunnel joining Valak Mountain to the Supply Convoy, as Bionis's arm partially rests on Sword Valley. After traversing a small part of it, the party gets their first sight of the sword and Galahad Fortress, and realize that ether from Bionis is being drawn into the sword, as fuel for Mechonis. There are no enemies here.

The Behemoth Nest (Japanese: , Behimosu no Su) is a location in . It is located on the second floor of Prison Island, and is only accessible on the second visit. It is accessed from the Battle Arena after Dickson makes the Arena drop a level with the party on it. It is inhabited by a pair of Sanjibal Behemoths. From this area the party can descend to the Kitchen.

Berserker (Japanese: , Bāsākā) is one of Reyn's arts in . It activates an aura that raises his strength by a large percentage, but decreases his Physical Defence by 25%. It also gives an area effect to Mad Taunt and his Auto-Attacks. The effect lasts for fifteen seconds. In , Nene can use this art.

Berserk Arduns are two normal enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Ardun family, and are found at level 16 north of Spiral Valley in Bionis' Leg. They normally accompany the Trainer Harmelon Unique Monster. They do not drop Treasure Chests but carry items that can be obtained using Riki's Yoink! ability. There is a Story Exclusive variant. There are two level 14 Berserk Arduns fought while rescuing Juju at Rho Oasis in Bionis' Leg.
is a Bipedal Enemy]] Bipedal Enemies are enemies in that walk on two legs, including flightless birds. [B] = Boss [U] = Unique Monster [Q] = Quest Exclusive Enemy [S] = Story Exclusive Enemy

Big Brogs (Japanese: , Biggu Guroggu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Brog family, and can be found at level 18 on Bionis' Leg in the marshes west of Spiral Valley and on the island west of Kasharpa Falls. They can drop the Brog Leg Meat needed for Material Quest 1.

The Bionis' Right Elbow (Japanese: , Kyoshin no migi hiji) is a location in . It is located on Valak Mountain east of but not connected to Valak Peak, and as its name implies it is located on Bionis approximately where its right elbow is. It is inhabited by Setor Eks, Monta Moramoras, Reef Nebulae, Latio Apis, and Corladio Apis. At night Lophos Moramoras replace the Monta Moramoras, and the Wandering Amon, a very high levelled Unique Monster, appears. There is also a water Ether Crystal deposit.

Bitter Pojics is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is given to the party by Norara during Unstoppable Berryjammy, and is made of three lots of Caterpile Vinegar that the party previously collected.

Bionis' Occipital (Japanese: , Kyoshin Kōtōbu) is a location in . It is located on the far left side of the Eryth Sea, which is also the back of Bionis' head. Prison Island floats directly above the center of Bionis' Occipital prior to Bionis' awakening.

Black Fog Deposits are common materials in . They can only be obtained from Eques Skyrays on the first visit to Prison Island or traded for with Talia in Alcamoth. According to their description, they are made from condensed lumps of fog which release black fog when struck.
Before the Final Battle (Japanese: , Saigo no Tatakai no Mae ni) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the Corridor of Silence on Prison Island, between Fiora and Shulk at pink affinity.

Blattas (Japanese: , Buratta) are cockroach-like creatures in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This species has the highest number of enemies, and tend to get aggressive at night. They can be found in all five regions. Most are weak and small in size, though, making them easy to deal with. In combat, they use physical and electric arts, or a physical counter spike. Only the feather appendage can be destroyed, which may drop a specific material determined by the color variants.
Black Butterfly is a Melee Art in . It deals Ether damage and inflicts Ether Res Down on the target. It also decreases the target's Aura duration.

The Behemoth's Shadows (Japanese: , Kyoei no Dōkutsu, Giant Shadow Cave) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, on the same outcropping as FN Site 420. As with all Unexplored Territories, the discovery of the Behemoth's Shadows yields an achievement ("The Dim of Behemoth's Shadows"). The Behemoth's Shadows is a large cave complex within the Delusian Mountains. It is a circular track with several chambers and levels. Clockwise from the cave's entrance is a small area filled with stone pillars and a small tunnel leading to a larger area filled with Cantors and Scintimures. Following the trail up leads to a subterranean lake filled with Sacrifoles and t

Beehive Rock (Japanese: , Bīhaibu Rokku) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, directly above the West Ibra Ravine and north of the Central Ibra Ravine. It is a grassy plain with a cavity in its centre. Bobora and Milly can be found here during Black Lifehold. Beehive Rock can be reached easily by Skell with a Flight Module, or by careful Skell jumping.

The Big Suid (Japanese: , Biggu Zūsu) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Suid family. During City Saviors, if route A is chosen, a level 16 big suid appears on Primordia's West Gate Plain and must be defeated. If route B is chosen during that mission, five level 22 – 28 big suids appear later during A Painful Lesson and must be defeated.

Bedrock Hold (Japanese: , Ganban Yōsai) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Ganglion stronghold located in north-west Primordia, south of FN Site 101. It can be reached by walking over the Lesser Gemini Bridge or by flight.

Blants (Japanese: , Barando) are a family of enemies in the , first appearing in . They resemble walking plants, with a large flower on their heads and Venus flytraps for arms. They are usually found near or in water. Blants come in pink and purple varieties, and they can appear burrowed in the ground before attacking the party. "Blants" do not exist as a species in the game files - they are classified as Squood (and are therefore Aquatic type enemies). This was rectified in , and are now classified as Terrestrial type enemies.

|-|XC2 = |-|TTGC = Binding Roots are Tree collectibles in and . They can be found in the Gormott Province, in particular at the Forestry Collection Point northwest of the Lascham Island Skip Travel Point, and in Gormott.

Big Catch Opportunity (Japanese: , Tairyō no Yokan damo~!!) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 3 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 80 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 20 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Ichthyology" and "Salvaging Mastery" Field Skills.

The Bipedal Crab Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission The Water City. It enables the purchase of Bipedal Crab Chili from the Tomi Fishmongers shop at Torigoth in the Gormott Province.

Beneath the Cloud Sea is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 5 star in Development Level. It will only become available after visiting the Empire of Mor Ardain for the first time. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector" and "Fortitude" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Char-Grilled Grumbird in Volty Butchers * Skywards by Titan in Maluria Antiques

Black Wing Dance (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Infinity Fans. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). When used, Morag slashes with her fans at her front. This art recycles Mòrag's Twin Moonblade.

Cooking Spices is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Empire of Mor Ardain, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Botany", "Transport Mastery" and "Agronomy" Field Skills.

Coocana is an NPC in . She is a Leftherian who can be found outside the Azure Schoolhouse on Fonsett Island in the Leftherian Archipelago. Speaking to her is required during Electra's Blade Quest Go for it, Electra!, where she requests Electra create lightning from outside the village to confirm whether light travels faster than sound. Doing so requires Level 5 "Electric Mastery", and Level 1 "Mastery of Thunder".

Cooking Display (Japanese: , Ryōri no Hatten) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 2 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Fleet of Foot", "Expeditionist" and "Nopon Wisdom" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Bright Samod at Rumbletum Canteen * Coral Nopon Chess Set at Nopox Hobby Store

Cooking Up a Feast (Japanese: , Gochisou wo Tsukurunda mo!) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Nopon Wisdom" and "Dumpling Pro" Field Skills.

Containing the Chaos is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya by talking to Kikina the Nopon in the Plaza of Reprieve at night, after Garfont Mercenaries reaches Merc Level 5. It is only made available when the nation has 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Earth Mastery", "Expeditionist" and "Fortitude" Field Skills.

Confidential Documents is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal from Seesee in the Residential Area, when the nation has at least 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector", "Clairvoyant Eye" and "Fortitude" Field Skills.
Colony 8 is a location in . It is a Kevesi Colony, and the former colony of Garvel. Shortly before the battle in Alfeto Valley, it was destroyed by Consul H.

Colony Chi was an Agnian Colony in . Its commander was All-Slayer Oleg. Colony Chi was responsible for wiping out an unknown Kevesi colony, with one survivor. However, Oleg's ruthless tactics nearly wiped out Colony Chi in the process, which led him to realize that his hubris had come close to destroying all he fought for. This led to him changing his name to "Teach" and becoming the commander of Colony Gamma in an attempt to escape his past.

The Colony Gamma Wreckage (Japanese: , Koronī Ganma no Zangai) is a location in , located across from the Colony 5 Wreckage in Vermilion Woods. It is the wreckage of Colony Gamma's Ferronis after its Flame Clock is destroyed by A. There is an Enemy Territory located here.

The Colony 5 Wreckage (Japanese: , Koronī 5 no Zangai) is a location in , located across from the Colony Gamma Wreckage in Vermilion Woods. It is the wreckage of Colony 5's Ferronis after its Flame Clock is destroyed by A.

Congregating Lives is a track from and , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track eight of disc eight from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track eight of disc nineteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. In , this track plays when Nia and Melia fight against Origin. In , this track plays when N grants Matthew the powers of his Sword of The End, and instructs him to combine it with his Ouroboros Knuckles to defeat Alpha.

Crystal Frogs (Japanese: , Kurisutaru Furoggu) are collectables in . They can be found in Valak Mountain. According to their description, they are frogs that collect fulgurite pieces and stick them all over their bodies.
Crushing Guarders (Japanese: , Desutoroigādā, Destroy Guarder) are weapons in . They are gunlances wielded by Reyn. They can be acquired by trading with Zain who can be found in Alcamoth.

Cratere Nebulae (Japanese: , Kuratēre Nebura) are enemies in . They are members of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 77 in the Kitchen, on the first floor of Prison Island. It can drop the Inferno Elements needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction.

Cunning Chilkins (Japanese: , Akuratsuna Chirukin) are four quest exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Chilkin family, and can be found at levels 42-44 near Bionis' Wrist on Valak Mountain. They are only encountered when initiating Bad Timing, and must be defeated to complete the quest. They drop the Aged Chilkin Hairs needed for A Token of Friendship.

Cumulus Danaemos (Japanese: , Sekiun no Daneimosu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Ekidno family, and can be found at level 41 on Khatorl Seal Island in Eryth Sea. It can drop Ekidno Jaw Gristles, which are needed for Getting Bigger!.

Crista Apis (Japanese: , Kurisuta Apisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Apis family, and can be found at level 42 on Valak Mountain in the Apis Lair. They can drop Apis Gold Nuggets, which are required for Material Quest 3.

Corladio Apis are enemies in . They are members of the Apis family, and can be found at level 42 on Valak Mountain in the Apis Lair. They can drop Apis Gold Nuggets, which are required for Material Quest 3.

Costa Aries (Japanese: , Kosuta Ariesu) are enemies in . They are members of the Aries family, and can be found at level 43 on Valak Mountain during the day. Groups of them can be found around Ignia Hill, accompanied by Zefa Ories. They can drop Frozen Aries Meat, two lots of which are needed for World's Strongest Flavour.

Crimson Egel Eyes are rare materials in . They can be obtained only from Gimran Egels on Prison Island and are not available for trade. According to their description, they are bloodshot eyes that have not slept for three days and some vitamins might pep them up.

Critical Rate is a stat in and . It is the probability that an attack will score a Critical Hit, increasing the amount of damage by 25%. A character's critical rate depends on the equipped weapon, and can be increased with Critical Up gems or by the use of certain Battle Arts.

Cursed Blattas (Japanese: , Kāsu Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 51-60 on a island in the west part of Primordia Waters.

Crazed Germivores (Japanese: , Maddo Burōsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Germivore family, and can be found at level 11-13 in Cauldros, on the island with FN Site 516.

DE913: Dieara (Japanese: , DE913: Diera) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Definian who appears on an island near the West Gate Plain in Primordia at the end of the Normal Mission Attack on Biahno Hills, where the party must battle her.

Crank Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Candid & Credible Gatling Gun. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission The Handy Ma-non. The Crank weapons available in-game are: * Storm Crank * Soldier Crank * Warrior Crank * Ophidian Crank * Destroyer Crank * Striker Crank * Delta Crank * Original Crank * Cosmic Crank * Nebulan Crank
Critical Power is a buff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases the damage of a character's critical hits.

Cool Off (Japanese: , Kūrudaun, Cooldown) is Sharla's Talent Art in . It can be activated at any time if Sharla's Talent Gauge is not empty, and is automatically activated when her Talent Gauge is full. While Cool Off is active, Sharla regenerates 3% of her maximum HP every second, but cannot move, attack, or use arts. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called Doze Off.

Core Crystals are objects in the , first introduced in . Drivers can resonate with Core Crystals by touching them to create and awaken Blades who endow their Driver with power and a weapon. They are collected throughout .

Crimson Derrick (Japanese: , Hiiro no Rongikepusu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Taos family and can be found at level 58, flying around the area between the Cape O-uru and the Jubilee Gate at the Cliffs of Morytha. It must be defeated in order to unlock Zenobia's level 5 Diabolic Zephyr, Vess's level 5 Thunderstrike and Mythra's level 5 Ray of Punishment Blade Specials.

Corinne's House (Japanese: , Korureru no Ie) is a Landmark in . It is located on Fonsett Island in the Leftherian Archipelago. It is the home of Corinne, who raised Rex when he was younger. The house features both a kitchen for Pyra to cook with, as well as functioning as an inn.

Crunchy Passion Fruits are Vegetable collectibles in . They can be found in the Empire of Mor Ardain, in particular from the two Collection Points at the Old City of Teddim, by coming from Ruined Laborers' Bridge near Decapitator Marvin. In the , Crunchy Passion Fruits can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.

Cubic Diamonds are Ore collectibles in . They can be found in the Leftherian Archipelago or the Empire of Mor Ardain, in particular from the Collection Point right after going up the stairs at Ruined Laborers' Bridge. Five of them are required for the quest Powered-Up Poppi. One is needed to refine Fast Blade Switch VI Aux Cores.

Crane Repairs (Japanese: , Kurēn no Shūri) is a Merc Mission in It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 1 star in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Electric Mastery" and "Industry Mastery" Field Skills.

Crane Protection (Japanese: , Kurēn wo Mamore) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild by talking to Lomlom, who works on piping outside of the Goldmouth Wheelhouse, when the nation has at least 3 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 80 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 20 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Ichthyology", "Industry Mastery" and "Water Mastery" Field Skills.

The Coralline Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission The Water City. It enables the purchase of Coralline Marimbas from the Soniarus Music shop at Torigoth in the Gormott Province.

Cuisine Researcher is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 3 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 1 hour, but it can be reduced down to 15 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist", "Info Collector" and "Production Mastery" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Whitebait-Samod Hotpot in Tatraty Fish * Jeweled Billiard Balls in Hobby Trappers * Musical Hair Clasp in Boldarde Textiles

Crafty Developments is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Production Mastery", "Fortitude" and "Botany" Field Skills. It rewards store contracts that unlock the following wares: * Astrology Made Simple in Biblio Paulio * Torigoth Snowpouch in Boldarde Textiles

Creature of the Depths (Japanese: , Shinkai ni Hisomu Mamono) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Argentum Trade Guild by talking to Karozze at the end of the metal deck path on the Bower Lounge level, when the nation has 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Dark Mastery", "Ichthyology" and "Electric Mastery" Field Skills.

Counter is a Skill RAM/Upgrade in . It grants Tora a physical Counter Spike that deals up to 200% of his Strength stat in damage every time he dodges or evades an attack. It can be used to customize Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ as an Aux Core equivalent. Poppi α is not compatible with this part. __TOC__
Crimson Moonblooms are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. It can also be purchased from the Colony Gamma Caravan, or produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Cross-Stamped Box is a Key Item in . It is obtained on the roof of Michiba Canteen in the City during Unsolved Riddle.
Cyma (Japanese: , Shima) is a character in who can be found in the City.

Coralie is a NPC in . She lives in the City and is friends with Moyshe. During The Path I Forge, she runs into Seeker after dropping her ring, and asks him and the party to help her find it. After they find it, she promises that in 10 years, she will visit Agnus Castle and see Seeker.

Daze is a status in and which stuns the target and removes auras (except for enemies' Crazed auras). While stunned, the target cannot dodge attacks, so attackers can hit the dazed target with 100% accuracy. Stunned targets have stars circle around their head. Critical damage increases by 25% (note: critical damage cannot be stacked with topple). When an enemy is dazed, its aggro will not increase. The daze duration for enemies is 2 seconds. Daze can also break the enemy's arts tag while the enemy is casting an art. This will subsequently cause the enemy to use a different art.

Death Lychees (Japanese: , Deddo Raichi, Dead Lychee) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found on Prison Island. According to their description, they have a sweetness to die for and pressing them creates a white juice that is like cream soda. Ten are required for one route of A Dauntless Trader.

Deadly Kiwis (Japanese: , Deddorī Kiui) are collectables in . They can be found on Prison Island. According to their description, they are black kiwis so cold that all the other fruits pale in comparison.

Dancing Squirrels (Japanese: , Odorisu) are collectables in . They can be found on Prison Island. According to their description, their green fur and love of dancing make them look like leaves in the breeze.

Deadly Medorlo (Japanese: , Shūen no Medeouro) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Licorne-type Telethia, and can be found at level 93 in the middle of Central Seal Island in the Eryth Sea, after the events in the Mechonis Core.

Deified Queens (Japanese: , Chinju no Kuīn) are three quest exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are part of the Queen family, and can be found on the roof of Exile Fortress in Satorl Marsh. Deified Queens first appear after placing the Giants' Mirror on the altar atop Exile Fortress during the quest The Giants' Treasure. They do not have to be fought when they appear, and indeed can safely be ignored entirely if the party is at level 38 or higher. If defeated, they can temporary respawn until the quest is completed. Then they will never reappear during future visits, instead being replaced by the much more powerful Eternal Palsadia.
Dark Claws are common materials in . They can be obtained from Babel Deinos, Gimran Egel, and Newgate Laia on Prison Island. Dark Claws are not otherwise obtainable.
Deinos Tongues are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from the Serene Imlaly and Babel Deinos in Prison Island. Deinos Tongues are not otherwise obtainable.

The Definians (デフィニア, Definia) are a race of beings in . They are a humanoid alien race; a tribe of women with high stealth skills and experts in infiltration by disguise, due to their ability to manipulate others' perception. They often use Ganglion weapons and equipment, and are responsible for many of the minor antagonisms of New Los Angeles.
Dadato (English dub: ) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Nopon and can be found on one island of the Floating Reef in Oblivia during Mia Grows Up.

Damage is a stat in Xenoblade Chronicles. It corresponds to the amount of HP lost when hit by an attack. A character will do damage on an opponent to kill them. Damage can be applied using different methods: # Auto-Attacks: attacking the enemy with weapons. Characters will perform these attacks automatically. This process can be quickened using Haste. # Using arts: a character's attack arts do more damage than an auto-attack. # Status attacks: these will slowly deplete opponents' HP. These can be Blaze, Chill, and others. Also sometimes referred to as Damage over Time or DoT attacks. The amount of damage dealt by a character's attack is based on the weapon's attack power, the character's Str

Decapitator Marvin (Japanese: , Kubiori no Bōn) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Igna family and can be found at level 33 at the Old City of Teddim by the Ruined Laborers' Bridge in the Empire of Mor Ardain. It must be defeated in order to unlock Zenobia's level 3 "The Indomitable" Affinity Reward.

Daram Isle (Japanese: , Daramu-tō) is a landmark in . It is an island located in the Rigitte Waters of the Leftherian Archipelago and connects to Baldotas Isle and the Orl Cloudway: Rigitte. There is a Salvage Point here.

Daily Training is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya by talking to Urbel, who sits on a crate at the top left of the Garfont Training Ground, when the nation has at least 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Water Mastery" and "Chivalry" Field Skills.

Dandes Salt Cave is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 80 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 20 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Fire Mastery", "Mineralogy" and "Earth Mastery" Field Skills.

Daedal Isle (Japanese: , Didāra-tō) is a location in , located in Erythia Sea. It is the remains of a large Leftherian Titan. The Tengate Ruins, Eternal Canopy, First Pillar Remnant, and Fifth Pillar Remnant can all be found on this island.

Dark Vollgulls are Normal Enemies in . They are Fogbeast Vollgulls, and can be found at level 54 at the Sullied Temple of Abitalia on the Aurora Shelf, and at level 45 at the Argan Cathedral Ruins and Kana Peak on the Black Mountains during Red Lightning.
The Data Unit FN093 is an Important Item in . It is collected north of FN Site 103 in Primordia during the course of Primordia Trailblazing 3 during Planetary Pioneer (Part I).
The Data Unit FN094 is an Important Item in . It is collected near Elephant's Trunk in Noctilum during the course of Noctilum Trailblazing 3 during Planetary Pioneer (Part II).
The Data Unit FN095 is an Important Item in . It is collected near FN Site 313 in Oblivia during the course of Oblivia Trailblazing 3 during Planetary Pioneer (Part III).
The Data Unit FN096 is an Important Item in . It is collected near FN Site 408 in Sylvalum during the course of Sylvalum Trailblazing 3 during Planetary Pioneer (Part IV).
The Data Unit FN097 is an Important Item in . It is collected near FN Site 505 in Cauldros during the course of Cauldros Trailblazing 3 during Planetary Pioneer (Part V).
The Deck (Japanese: , Kanpan) is a landmark in . It is located in the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles. There is a teleporter that can transport the party to BLADE Tower.

Defending is an enemy-exclusive buff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Defending makes the enemy unable to move and attack, but reduces the amount of damage taken from attacks and makes it immune to mobility-impairing debuffs. However, while appendages take reduced damage, their health meter is reduced at the same rate as normal, making it easier to destroy appendages without killing the enemy. Defending is usually gained by using a Battle Art named Guard. An enemy in a Defending state hunkers down and protects its face using its arms if it has any.

Demon King Dragonia (Japanese: , Akuma-ō Doragonia) is a quest exclusive enemy in . It is a member of the Dragon family, and can be found at level 99 at the Hope Farm in Colony 6 during Defend Colony 6 - Demon. It cannot be seen at first, but it will be seen flying down to the ground as the party gets closer to its location, in the same way as Avalanche Abaasy does. It will drop the Demonic Everflame needed for Replica Monado 4.

Dorsiar Lizards (Japanese: , Dorushie Rizado) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Lizard family, and can be found at level 91-92 north of Bone Corridor in Tephra Cave. They are a source of slotted M100 Helms. They are the only enemy that drops Lizard Moon Jewels, which are required for Friendship Tokens.

The Demon Pavlovsk (Japanese: , Makai-jū Pavurofusuku) is a boss in . It is a member of the Behemoth family, and can be found at level 78 in the Battle Arena in Prison Island, after defeating the Obelis Obart in the Arena. The Demon Pavlovsk is the only boss that drops a Treasure Chest.

Destroyer Salvacion (Japanese: , Inmetsu no Sarubashion) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 59 on the 2F Observation Post in Mechonis Field. Nearby enemies may join the battle.

The Digit 1 Crevasse (Japanese: , Oyayubi no Sakeme) is a location in . It is located on the Fallen Arm, west of the Giant Mechon Debris, between the knuckles of Digit 1 and Digit 2. Tiny blue and orange butterflies and red winged dragonflies fly around the area in the day, and glowflies can be seen at night.

Dirty Snow Wings are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from various Chilkins on Valak Mountain. Dirty Snow Wings are also available via trading with Yura before he moves to Colony 6 if he has not before the events of Mechonis Core. According to their description, they are snow wings that are all dirty, so they are not really of any value.
Dickson's Amulet is a material in Xenoblade Chronicles. For unknown reasons, it was cut from the game. It was most likely intended to be dropped by Dickson after he is defeated on Prison Island.
Dismemberer is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when an enemy appendage is destroyed.

The Dorian Caravan (English dub: ) (Japanese: , Dorian Kyaraban) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Nopon Caravan situated on an island in Lake Basel in Oblivia. It must be visited during BFFs, Fitting In, Mia Grows Up and Sparking a Smile.

The Delusians North Summit (Japanese: , Kita Meimō-san Chōjō) is a landmark in . It is the plain atop the northern Delusian mountain located in Sylvalum, north of Hardheart Canyon. The Delusians North Summit BC is located here. The Blood-Soaked Beast Fur can be found here during Turf War, and it must be visited during Chapter 10 and Chapter 13 (Act 2).

The Demon's Pocket (Japanese: , Dēmonzu Poketto) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a cave located in Oblivia. It can be reached by flying along the bottom of the Yawning Giant, southeast of FN Site 306, or by gliding through the air with a Hraesvelg.

Don Dondon (Japanese: , Dōn) is a Nopon in . He is Bana's father, and the true leader of Lindwurm. After the quest Bana's Revenge, he can be found in the Argentum Trade Guild, powering the generator with his son.

Domko (Japanese: , Domeniko) is an NPC in . Domko is an Urayan who can be found at the Fonsa Myma Port in the Kingdom of Uraya with his Animal Common Blade. If Floren is in the party and has got level 4 "Beguiling Charms" Field Skill, he will give a common Moon Cube.

Devastating Tremor (Japanese: Resshingeki) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using Rockrending Gauntlets. It can be obtained upon New Game Plus, after finishing the game and installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0). This art recycles Mòrag's Sneak Hit.

Desserts Delivered 2 is a DLC Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya after completing the DLC Quest The Trendy Patissier. The time required to complete this mission is 30 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 7 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Expeditionist", "Transport Mastery" and "Superstrength" Field Skills. It uniquely awards more Trust than other normal Merc Missions. It also rewards Lunana Smoothies every time it is completed.

Devoted Marigold Nia (Japanese: ) is a DLC Aux Core in . It increases damage dealt by 55% when the Affinity between Driver and Blade is at max. It also changes Nia's Blade form appearance when she equips the core, granting her the yellow color scheme of her Driver form. It can be purchased at the DLC shop Noponstone Exchange after Chapter 7 for 20 Flawless Noponstones in the Land of Challenge obtained after completing a Challenge Battle, available as downloadable content from the Challenge Battle Mode Pack of the Expansion Pass. Its effect is functionally identical to the Affinity MAX Atk VI Aux Core. The Magical Pink Pandoria and Mermaid-Blue Pandoria DLC Aux Cores have slightly weaker vers

The Dispare Ropl (Japanese: , Disupea Ryibura) is a Story and Quest Exclusive Enemy in . It is a member of the Ropl family and can be found at level 16 in Gormott, near Valafum Hill. It must be defeated during the Story Quest Power Unimaginable. As with all Quest-exclusive Enemies in , the Dispare Ropl drops no items, only gold.

Dolala is an young Nopon NPC in , and can first be found at Yanchik Harbor before moving to downstairs in Spefan Inn in Auresco of the Kingdom of Torna. Dolala is very impressed with the party and wants to be a powerful Driver too later in life. Dolala gives no quests, and Community is gained upon speaking to Dolala once level 4 Community is required to progress the plot. Nalsaz and Clemens share this condition.

Doom is a status effect in and . It is similar to Instant Death in . It is a party debuff that causes the incapacitation of Drivers, once five seconds pass from the moment when it gets inflicted. It has a chance to be resisted 20% of the time by default. Unlike with other debuffs, it has no additional visual indicators outside of the "Doom" debuff tag briefly appearing next to the afflicted character.
Doublecrag Gate (Japanese: , Sōgan no Mon) is a Landmark in . It is located on Corne Island in Erythia Sea.
The Demihuman Gutter (Japanese: , Ajin Rengoku) is a Landmark in , located in Rebellion Cave in Erythia Sea. The party's Ouroboros powers are restricted here, which prevents Interlinking.

Digging Sandfly Fossils are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region. They can also be produced from the Atoll Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They are fossils of Digging Sandflies from the Leftherian Archipelago.
Devilflyer Moramoras are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Moramora family, and can be found at level 62 at Brasa Geothermal Belt in the Erythia Sea.

Determination (Japanese: , Ditāminēshon) is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Yumsmith class. When used, it provides a stance to the user that greatly increases their combat capabilities while they are in a field effect. This includes the field effects provided by Energy Grenade or Roasty-Toasty, neither of which provide buffs to allies.

Diastone Feris are two Bosses in . They are Fogbeast Feris that are fought at level 1 on Corne Island in Erythia Sea during a flashback, where they attack Matthew and Na'el. They are the lowest level enemies in .

Dry Lemons (Japanese: , Dorai Remon) are collectables in . They can be found in Prison Island and Colony 6. According to their description, they are so cold that the juice seems frozen and they are so delicious that they do not bother someone who eats them.

Dragon King Alcar (Japanese: , Ryūō Arukatorazu, lit. Dragon-king Alcatraz) is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Dragon family, and can be found at level 79 in the Corridor of Silence on Prison Island during the Story Quest Path to the Top. It appears immediately after activating the Dragon Summon that rings the bell on the Basverg Belfry. It is fought just before the battle with Dickson. This enemy deals Spike Damage. It must be defeated to complete the second objective of Path to the Top, and it will drop the Dragon's Eye that must be fitted into the Altar to complete the story quest.
Ekidnos (Japanese: , Ekidona, lit. Echidna) are a family of flying enemies in the .

The Dragon's Eye is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is needed during Path to the Top and obtained from the Dragon King Alcar after defeating it in the Corridor of Silence. It must be fitted into the Altar to raise the transporter that leads to the topmost level of Prison Island, the Prison Terrace.

Drakos Telethia (Japanese: , Dorakosu Tereshia) are enemies in . They are Drakos-type members of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 74 in Bionis' Interior. One can periodically be found flying over the large platform south of the Terminal Vein.

The Dragon Summon is a switch in . It is located at the top of Basverg Belfry on Prison Island. Activating it rings a large bell, causing Dragon King Alcar to appear in front of the altar in the Corridor of Silence. The boss must be defeated to obtain an item which is needed for Path to the Top.

Earth is a planet that appears in the , and in flashbacks in the . So far, in separate realities sharing the same multiverse, there have been two separate versions of Earth, as well as two distinct strands of its human inhabitants; while both started out as slightly more advanced versions of the modern society in the real world's 21st century, both humanities ended up with vastly different fates and heritages.
East Gate (Japanese: , Īsuto Gēto) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the Administrative District area of New Los Angeles and connects the city to East Gate Plain.

Eckart, the Indestructible (, Kōtetsu no Ekkaruto) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Cinicula, and can be found at level 50 on a raised hill northeast of the Grieving Plains in Primordia.

East Ibra Ravine (Japanese: , Ibura Keikoku Tōbu) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Oblivia, at the eastern end of the continent. It is a narrow canyon filled with high-leveled insectoid indigens.

Dragonbone Promontory (Japanese: , Ryūkotsu-misaki) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Cauldros, northeast of the Adder Byroad and north of the Ternion Fork. There is a teleport here to the lines of the Forgotten Mining Frigates directly above, which is inhabited by two Milsaadi Hunters.

The Drop Shaft (Japanese: , Tateana Kūdō) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is an enclosed shaft with two lower areas and a cave, located in Primordia, just south of the Arendt Bridge. The entrance is located on the upper crag area of Talon Rock Summit and as such, access requires a Skell with a flight module equipped. A mix of low level and level 60 enemies inhabit the interior cavern, as well as the level 69 Tyrant Necro, the Cavelord. During the daytime the Drop Shaft's namesake entrance is guarded by the level 90 Tyrant Elvira, the Talondrake. There is also a level 4 archaeological Treasure Box in the cave.

Eisen, the Ebon Rock (Japanese: , Kurokō no Aizen) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Petramand family. It can be found at level 51 on a rock in the lava river east of Ruined City of O'rrh Sim in Cauldros at night. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Eisen, the Ebon Rock.

Dual Guns Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Sakuraba Industries Dual Guns. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Fauna category of the Primordia Collectopedia. Dual Guns II Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Sakuraba Industries Dual Guns. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Alien Nation alongside the Haven Series.
